rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so there is no evidence about whether RNA, image, multiprofile aggregation, or fusion provides useful signal. This experiment tests the simplest RNA-only baseline using a single profile and PCA representation. It is the best first use of budget because it establishes a low-confounding reference point for later comparisons with multiprofile RNA, image-only, and multimodal configurations.

The only completed result is a weak RNA-only PCA single-profile baseline, so it is unclear whether the image modality contains useful signal. Testing image-only ResNet50 with the same single-profile setting establishes a simple image baseline without confounding effects from aggregation or fusion. This reduces uncertainty about the key design choice of whether image data should be used at all, and creates a necessary reference point before deciding whether multimodal fusion is worth testing.

RNA single-profile PCA is the strongest completed result (acc 0.485, F1 0.464), while image ResNet is weak (acc 0.208, F1 0.172). The key uncertainty is whether the RNA signal can be improved by using multiple profiles with a simple aggregation before adding more complex encoders or fusion. config_002 keeps the same RNA encoder and modality as config_001 and tests the minimal multiprofile setting with avgpool, establishing a multiprofile PCA baseline and clarifying whether profile aggregation helps. This is a focused, high-information exploitation of the promising RNA direction under a limited budget.

RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool improved strongly from 48.5% to 59.1% accuracy, showing that multiprofile RNA aggregation is promising. The key uncertainty is whether a more expressive transformer aggregation outperforms simple avgpool for the same RNA representation. config_003 tests this by changing only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding model setting, profile setting, and RNA encoder fixed. This is the best next experiment because it builds on the strongest evidence, isolates an important design choice, and will inform whether transformer aggregation is worth using in later multimodal extensions.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile RNA with PCA and avgpool is clearly best (config_002: acc 0.591, F1 0.573), while single-profile RNA and transformer aggregation are weaker, and image-only ResNet is poor. The key remaining uncertainty is whether a stronger RNA representation can improve the already promising multiprofile avgpool setting. config_008 changes only the RNA encoder from PCA to scGPT while keeping profile setting and aggregation fixed, so it cleanly tests representation quality. This is a focused exploitation of the current best direction and more informative than moving to image or multimodal settings with weak image evidence.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool is the best configuration (accuracy 0.591, F1 0.573), clearly outperforming single-profile RNA and transformer aggregation, while image-only ResNet50 is weak (accuracy 0.208). The key uncertainty is whether image features can complement the strong RNA baseline in a multimodal model. config_018 tests this by adding ResNet50 image features to the best known RNA setup while keeping profile setting, RNA encoder, and aggregation fixed, using simple concat fusion as a baseline. This is the best next experiment because it directly extends the strongest evidence, isolates the contribution of adding image information as much as possible, and will clarify whether multimodal fusion is worth further investment under the limited budget.

The strongest completed result is config_018, a multimodal multiprofile PCA + ResNet50 model with avgpool and concat fusion, reaching 0.6186 accuracy and 0.6103 F1, modestly above the best RNA-only multiprofile avgpool result. This suggests the current multimodal direction is promising, but fusion method is still untested: only concat has been evaluated. config_019 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted while keeping the same model, profile, RNA encoder, image encoder, and aggregation. It directly tests whether weighted fusion can improve on the best-known setting or whether concat is already sufficient. This is the best next use of budget because it exploits the strongest evidence while isolating one important design choice, giving both high expected performance and clear diagnostic value before exploring image encoders, aggregations, or alternative RNA encoders.

The current best configuration is config_019, a multimodal multiprofile model with PCA RNA, ResNet50 image, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion, achieving the highest validation accuracy and F1. Image-only ResNet50 was weak, suggesting the image branch may be a limiting factor. config_025 keeps the best-known profile, RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion settings while replacing ResNet50 with ImageNet ViT-L, directly testing whether a stronger image representation improves performance. This is the best next experiment because it is a one-variable comparison that exploits the strongest current direction while reducing uncertainty about an important untested design choice.

The strongest completed result is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted; 0.639 accuracy / 0.620 F1), with weighted fusion outperforming concat and multiprofile avgpool outperforming transformer in the RNA-only comparison. The key unresolved question in this best branch is whether transformer aggregation can improve over avgpool when fused with image features. config_021 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the otherwise best settings, directly isolating the aggregation effect in the current promising multimodal setting. Under a limited budget, this is the best next experiment because it is a minimal, high-information extension of the current best: if it improves, it identifies a better aggregation; if not, it confirms avgpool and lets later experiments focus on RNA encoder or image encoder choices.

The strongest evidence is that the best configuration so far is config_019: multimodal, multiprofile, PCA RNA, ResNet50, avgpool, weighted fusion, with validation accuracy 0.639 and F1 0.6197. Transformer aggregation appears harmful, weighted fusion is better than concat, and ResNet50/ViT are similar, with ResNet50 slightly better. The main remaining uncertainty in this strong setting is whether a learned RNA encoder can improve on PCA, since RNA-only scGPT was weaker than PCA but scVI has not been tested. config_031 tests scVI_n200 while keeping the same multimodal, multiprofile, ResNet50, avgpool, and weighted-fusion design, so it isolates the RNA representation choice. This is the best next experiment because it is a clean one-factor extension of the current best direction: it may find a better model or efficiently confirm that PCA is already sufficient before spending budget on more complex RNA encoders.
